strategy_highlights: **Work and orders for companies in the Espace Mittelland** The business year 2006 in brief

Your bank again achieved a good result in the past year and has come a further step closer to achieving its ten-year goal. After four years, free cash flow with a total of CHF 513 million is beyond the target range. Annual profit prior to taxes and prior to profit from the partial disposal of a participation increased again in the past year for the fourteenth time in a row. On the basis of 123’s positive result and its solid foundation, we propose the tenth dividend increase in a row from CHF 3.50 to CHF 3.80 as well as a nominal value repayment of CHF 5.00 per registered share.

At the last general meeting, we put you, our stockholders, at the center. With a total of 56,000 coowners, the bank is among the first ten Swiss companies in terms of broad public ownership. This establishment in the public with the canton of Berne as its main stockholder forms the basis for a successful development of the bank. Many small and mediumsized companies in the Espace Mittelland that function as suppliers for 123 and regularly execute orders for our bank also benefit from this fact.

At this year’s general meeting of stockholders, we will present to you our regular suppliers in the Espace Mittelland. Some of these are contained in the present brochure. 123 contributes to a creation of value and to the strengthening and independent development of our economic environment and living space through this type of business relationship with small and medium-sized companies.
123 has set itself a long-term financial goal: it aims to achieve free cash flow amounting to CHF 800 million to 1 billion within ten years (from 2003 until 2012).

After four years, added value with a total of CHF 513.2 million is beyond the target range. Focusing on two core businesses and governance that aims for a bank with a strong balance sheet structure, robust refinancing, optimized earning power and a stronger equity position have once again proven to be the right strategy. Annual profit prior to taxes and prior to profit from the partial sale of a participation increased again in the past year for the fourteenth time in a row: in 2006 profits were up 4.3 percent to CHF 126.4 million. In addition, the bank registered an extraordinary after-tax profit amounting to CHF 42.5 million resulting from the sale of shares in BKW FMB Energie AG, which was allocated in full to reserves for general banking risks. Annual net profit (after deducting tax expenses amounting to CHF 46.6 million) was CHF 92.2 million, up CHF 7.1 million over the prior year.
